gaps.question: mfa_remote
gaps.current: No MFA on remote access, or RDP open to the internet
gaps.recommended: Yes - MFA on all remote access and no exposed RDP
gaps.note: Remote-access compromise is the most common ransomware entry route in Coveware's 2025 data, and Coalition reports businesses with internet-exposed RDP are 2.5x more likely to file a claim. Missing MFA here is a typical knock-out.

gaps.question: backups
gaps.current: Off-site / cloud copy reachable with normal admin credentials
gaps.recommended: Immutable or offline copy, separate credentials, full restore tested in the last 12 months
gaps.note: Sophos 2024: when backups were compromised, victims were almost twice as likely to pay (67% vs 36%), recovered within a week half as often (25% vs 46%), and had 8x the median recovery cost. Marsh lists secured, encrypted, tested backups as a key control.

gaps.question: mfa_email
gaps.current: Partly - some users, or MFA optional
gaps.recommended: Yes - enforced for all users (conditional access / security defaults)
gaps.note: MFA on email is close to a universal requirement on SMB applications. At-Bay states any policy covering ransomware is highly likely to require MFA and that coverage levels depend on which services are enrolled; Marsh notes firms lacking key controls face non-renewal or ransomware limitations.

gaps.question: edr
gaps.recommended: 100% coverage, monitored 24/7 (MDR / SOC)
gaps.note: EDR is among the controls Marsh found most associated with fewer incidents and is one of the three most frequently recommended by insurers; many carriers require it for larger SMBs.

gaps.question: mfa_privileged
gaps.recommended: Yes - all privileged accounts, separate admin accounts
gaps.note: Marsh lists privileged access management with EDR and MFA as the three controls insurers most often recommend; ransomware supplementals ask about admin MFA and separate admin accounts.

gaps.question: email_security
gaps.recommended: Yes - advanced filtering and DMARC p=quarantine/reject
gaps.note: Email filtering is on Marsh's list of priority controls and email is the entry route for over a third of ransomware incidents in Sophos' data.

gaps.question: training
gaps.recommended: Yes - at least quarterly, with phishing simulations
gaps.note: Almost every application asks about training, but the strongest effect data (KnowBe4: click rates down 86% after 12 months) comes from a vendor's own simulations.

gaps.question: ir_plan
gaps.recommended: Yes - written and tested in the last 12 months
gaps.note: Marsh's 2025 study ranks IR planning among the top control areas; IBM reports lower average breach costs for firms with an IR team and tested plan (correlational).

gaps.question: payment_verification
gaps.recommended: Yes - documented, enforced, dual approval above a threshold
gaps.note: BEC and funds-transfer fraud are 58-60% of Coalition's claims. Social-engineering cover is typically sublimited and applications ask about call-back verification, but no public study quantifies the effect.

gaps.question: patching
gaps.recommended: Within 7 days
gaps.note: In this repo's KEV analysis, half of exploited CVEs published since 2022 were listed as exploited within 7 days of publication. Marsh found 7-day patching associated with ~2x lower incident probability, but only 24% of organisations achieve it.

gaps.question: eol_systems
gaps.current: Yes, but isolated / segmented with compensating controls
gaps.recommended: No
gaps.note: Unsupported systems cannot be patched, so applications ask about them directly.

gaps.question: asset_inventory
gaps.recommended: Yes, automated and current
gaps.note: Underpins every other answer (EDR coverage %, patch compliance), so underwriters ask for it, but its direct loss effect is not quantifiable from public data.

gaps.question: encryption
gaps.recommended: Yes, enforced by policy
gaps.note: Encrypted lost devices generally fall under HIPAA and state breach-law safe harbours. Theft/loss is part of the non-malicious breach share the model does not change, so this answer is scored but not simulated.

gaps.question: vendor_access
gaps.recommended: Yes
gaps.note: DBIR 2025: third-party involvement in 30% of breaches, double the prior year.

gaps.question: logging
gaps.recommended: Yes
gaps.note: Without logs, forensics takes longer and breach scope often must be assumed worst-case (notify everyone).
